fixed.what: Fixed the round-1 regression in resolveEnd's {bars} branch (tools/film/plan/compile.mjs). The old edit-0 rule `pickup = bp < -1e-6 || inT <= 1e-9; base = pickup ? ceil(bp) : bp` is replaced by four ordered cases. tol = COMPILE_DEFAULTS.barLineTolBeats (new constant, 0.5) × grid.period, i.e. half a beat. (1) Pickup: the shot starts more than tol before the first downbeat (bp < 0 and inT − barTime(0) < −tol). It counts from the next downbeat, ceil(bp). (2) On a bar line: |inT − barTime(round(bp))| ≤ tol. It counts from that bar, round(bp). (3) Edit 0 more than tol inside a bar counts from the next downbeat, ceil(bp). (4) Any other mid-bar start keeps its length. Deliberate deviation from the brief: tol is half a beat, not 'a few ms'. A few ms would leave the exact scenario the checker reported still broken. In that scenario the downbeat is at 14.98 s and offsetSec is 15.0 (copied from analyze's one-decimal mmss), which is 20 ms past. Rounding can be off by up to 50 ms. For starts that are not at edit 0, half a beat gives the same cuts as the old keep-length plus nearest-beat rule. So the only change is for edit-0 starts up to half a beat past a downbeat: the first shot is now n bars minus δ, not n+1 bars minus δ. Results: offset 8, 8.001, 8.002, 7.998 and 8.01 on a grid at 0 now cut at 8/16/20, where 8.001/8.002/8.01 used to give 10/18/22. In the checker's probe2 (offset 15.0), v1 now ends on bar 9, not bar 10, and the trim warning is gone. 0.3 s into a bar at 120 BPM still counts from the next downbeat. A pickup with the first downbeat at 0.51 s gives 8.5/16.5/20.5. I also rewrote the header Rules bullet and the inline comment to match. Tests: added 3 checks to tests/film_plan_compile.test.mjs that execute every branch. (a) The brief's four cases: offsetSec 8 (on), 8.002 (2 ms after), 7.998 (2 ms before), and a real pickup (t0 0.51, offset 0). For each, every cut is within half a frame of song bar k+4, k+8, k+10, snap is 'bar', there are no warnings, and the first {bars:4} is 8 s. fixed.what: Rewrote three comments to state the real rule: the module header camera paragraph, the DRONE_PRESETS rollLimitDeg doc and the createDrone Guarantees block. The rule: the horizon-roll follow error, measured the short way across ±180° against the target's own roll, is pulled back inside ±rollLimitDeg while both camera and target are within 72° of level. The correction shares the follow's maxRateDeg budget, so the bound is soft (a target rolling faster than maxRate out-runs it). The target's deliberate roll is never clamped, and the limit never snaps or turns the long way; 180 turns it off.

Rewrote the old F5 roll check. It asserted a snap ('back inside ±45° at once'), which conflicts with the rate budget. It now asserts four things: the deliberate 80° roll is carried with error ≤ lim; every frame turns ≤ maxRate/30; after the 80° snap to level the error never grows; and the error is inside ±45° within ⌈35°/maxRate⌉+2 frames. Added three new checks. (1) A synthetic target roll 60°→300° at 1.2× and 1.45× maxRate, in both directions, at 24/30/60 fps on cinema/heavy/indoor, with the target's r fed wrapped so it crosses ±180°. Asserts: never faster than maxRate, the camera never rolls back against the target (no long way), it crosses the seam itself, error stays within the rate-deficit bound, and it settles below 0.5°. (2) Camera settled at ±170° while the target jumps to ∓110° (80° through the seam), on default presets and with rotSmoothSec 3. Asserts: ≤ maxRate, forward through the seam only, error never grows, the limit pulls the sluggish follow inside ±45° within ⌈35°/maxRate⌉+2 frames, and with rollLimitDeg 180 that takes more than twice as long, which proves the limit engages. (3) fpv.fpv-flip (±) and drone.canyon-run with roll ±3.0 and maxBankDeg 60 on a winding path, on cinema/heavy/indoor at 24/30/60 fps. Asserts: ≤ maxRate, the flip's roll travel is ±360° ±2° with no unwinding, canyon roll error < 10°, and the limited flight's error never exceeds rollLimitDeg 180 + 0.5°. Against the round-1 code (scratch copy /tmp/claude-1000/r2-drone/cur), all 4 roll checks FAIL: a 35.4° snap in one frame, −1.2° rolled back the long way, a 58° jump away from the target with a permanent 138° mirror error, and 7.7°/frame on fpv-flip. The score is the distance from the hit to the placement's vertical axis segment divided by its radius, so lower means closer to the middle; it no longer uses surface distance, which was 0 for every capsule containing the point. Because a faded key now implies the hit lies inside that placement's radius, sensors' seenThrough inherits the guarantee and sensors.js needed no change. So a hit on a boulder near a catalogued tree is attributed to the TREE.
